browserEvidence: curl GET https://dos.zone/the-secret-of-monkey-island/ -> HTTP 200, text/html; charset=utf-8, 37819 bytes. Saved headers: no X-Frame-Options; Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors names dos.zone and its own CDN only, so the host refuses framing from the Gameflex origin. Page HTML carries the js-dos launch UI markup ("Install" prompt, Fullscreen control, js-dos/latest/js-dos.css reference and the .jsdos bundle URL //cdn.dos.zone/custom/dos/monkey-island-1.jsdos). installPrompt=true, jsDosCss=true. Rendered launch UI only - no emulator session was started and no gameplay was observed. HEAD https://cdn.dos.zone/custom/dos/monkey-island-1.jsdos -> HTTP 200 (headers only; bundle was not downloaded or executed).
requirements: Desktop browser with keyboard and mouse; emulated DOS release.
issues: LucasArts title distributed by a third-party emulation host - rights status needs review.
Which release (EGA vs VGA, floppy vs CD talkie) is bundled was not confirmed.
The page description string is malformed ("On The Secret of Monkey Island is available..."), i.e. host copy is templated.

CSP frame-ancestors allows https://dos.zone and its own CDN but no third-party origin - embedding this page in the Gameflex player (another origin) is blocked by the host today, so an in-page js-dos embed or licensed bundle would be required.
Only a launch UI was verified: no emulator session, no save behaviour and no performance measurement were performed.
Version/edition of the hosted bundle is unknown: the .jsdos file was HEAD-probed only and never downloaded or executed, so build contents are unconfirmed.
Host page advertises virtual mobile controls; no touch-device session was run, so mobile play is a host claim only.
researchMethod: Public HTTPS fetch of https://dos.zone/top-games/ (HTTP 200, 1,666,503 bytes) for the source list; per-page curl fetch (no credentials, no login) recording status line, headers and raw HTML; HEAD probe of the recorded .jsdos bundle URL (headers only). Imported into research/candidates.json via scripts/research-db.mjs import from research/dos-top-expansion.json; artUrl downloaded and byte-validated in the same run (receipt: research/dos-expansion-artwork.json). No emulator session was started.
